newsitem.title: POLAND: Union Banka wants to buy Polish bank - paper.
newsitem.headline: Union Banka wants to buy Polish bank - paper.

text.p: The Czech bank Union Banka AS wants to buy a majority stake in Poland's Bank Przemyslowy SA, the Gazeta Wyborcza daily said on Tuesday.

It quoted Bank Przemyslowy's president Jerzy Fornalczyk as saying that the aquisition would help the Lodz-based bank broaden its activities above a regional scale by servicing trade between Poland and the Czech Republic.
"The heads of both institutions (Bank Przemyslowy SA and Union Banka) want bank Przemyslowy to become a financial institution on an inter-regional scale," Fornalczyk said.
"In the future it would have branches not only in Poland and the Czech republic but also in Slovakia and Hungary," he was quoted as saying.

The paper said Union Banka, based in the eastern town of Ostrava near the Polish border, would more than double the capital of Bank Przemyslowy from the current 15.3 million zlotys and could issue new shares for its clients later.
It said Bank Przemyslowy's main shareholder was currently the Lodz local authority, with a 17-percent stake.
The paper said the Polish bank, which has four branches, had been making losses since 1995.
No one at Bank Przemyslowy was immediately available for comment.
